findings.body:
The Unreleased entry claims an "API migration in scripts/pack.js", but `scripts/pack.js` is not part of this PR and does not exist in the repository (tree only has `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, and `CHANGELOG.md`). tar-stream 3 is a major bump with breaking API changes; documenting a completed migration that was not shipped will mislead anyone relying on the changelog.

Either add the real call-site migration to this PR, or change the bullet to record only the dependency pin bump (and note that call sites still need migration if/when they exist).

Major bump of `tar-stream` from `^2.2.0` to `^3.1.6` with no corresponding call-site updates in the same PR. The PR description says call sites were migrated; none appear in the diff. If this package is consumed with tar-stream 2-era pack/extract usage elsewhere, those sites will break at runtime once 3.x resolves.

Confirm there are no remaining tar-stream 2 call patterns, or include the migration (e.g. the claimed `scripts/pack.js`) before treating this as complete.

summary:
## Verdict

Major dependency bump is incomplete: the changelog and PR description claim a tar-stream 2→3 API migration in `scripts/pack.js`, but that file is not in the diff and does not exist in the repository.

## Narrative

`package.json` and `package-lock.json` correctly move `tar-stream` from 2.2.0 to 3.1.6. tar-stream 3 is a major release with breaking stream/API changes, so a real consumer would need call-site updates. This tree has no `scripts/` directory and no imports of `tar-stream` at all — only the version pins and a changelog bullet that asserts the migration already happened.

That makes the release note actively misleading for anyone reading Unreleased: it documents work that was not shipped. Before merge, either land the actual `scripts/pack.js` (or equivalent) migration in this PR, or rewrite the changelog to state that only the dependency pin moved and call sites still need review.

Lockfile version string matches `package.json` (^3.1.6 → locked 3.1.6), so the lockfile presence itself is fine; contents were omitted from review by policy.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
